/-!
# Erdős Problem 234

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/234](https://www.erdosproblems.com/234)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Real Set
open scoped NNReal

namespace Erdos234

/--
Is it true that for all `c ≥ 0`, the density `f c` of integers for which
`(p (n + 1) - p n) / log n < c` exists and is a continuous function of `c`?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_234 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ f : ℝ≥0 → ℝ, Continuous f ∧
    ∀ c : ℝ≥0, HasDensity {n : ℕ | primeGap n / log n < c} (f c) := by
  sorry

end Erdos234

reformulations.difference: `primeGap n := Nat.nth Nat.Prime (n + 1) - Nat.nth Nat.Prime n` uses 0-indexed primes (`nth Prime 0 = 2`), so the Lean set `{n | primeGap n / log n < c}` is, in the source's 1-indexed notation (p_1 = 2), {n : (p_{n+2} - p_{n+1}) / log n < c}, whereas the source has {n : (p_{n+1} - p_n) / log n < c}. Each gap is normalised by the log of an index one smaller than in the source. In addition, n = 0, 1 get the Lean junk value x/0 = 0, so they belong to the set iff c > 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The claim covers every c >= 0 at once and requires a continuous density function; as a whole, that claim is unchanged by the index shift. Let T_c be the Lean set and M_c = {m : d_{m+1} / log(m+1) < c}, the source set moved down by one. Moving a set by one, or changing finitely many elements, does not change natural density. For m >= 2, log m <= log(m+1) gives T_c \ M_c ⊆ {1}. For every c' > c, c·log(m+1) <= c'·log m holds for all large m, because log(m+1) - log m <= 1/m and log m >= 1; hence M_c \ T_{c'} is finite. So T_c ⊆ M_c ⊆ T_{c'} up to finitely many elements, for all c' > c. If the Lean densities F(c) exist with F continuous, right-continuity squeezes the density of M_c to F(c). Conversely, if the source densities G(c) exist with G continuous, left-continuity (for c > 0) squeezes the density of T_c to G(c). At c = 0 both sets are empty and both densities are 0. The same f therefore works on both sides. Machine-checked as `Review.erdos_234_rhs_iff_source` (general lemma `Review.shift_equiv`, for any g : ℕ → ℕ) in /workspace/review/equiv.lean. It uses only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, with no sorry, and it states the file's right-hand side verbatim against the source's statement with 1-indexed primes p k := nth Prime (k - 1).

review.notes:
No findings. The source text, confirmed live on erdosproblems.com/latex/234 on 2026-09-23, is: \"For every $c\\geq 0$ the density $f(c)$ of integers for which \\[\\frac{p_{n+1}-p_n}{\\log n}< c\\] exists and is a continuous function of $c$. See also [5].\" Checks performed:
(1) The elaborated statement is `True ↔ ∃ f : ℝ≥0 → ℝ, Continuous f ∧ ∀ c, {n | ↑(primeGap n) / Real.log ↑n < ↑c}.HasDensity (f c)`, where `answer(sorry)` defaults to `True` at Prop. The comparison is in ℝ, and `c` is coerced from ℝ≥0.
(2) `HasDensity` with the default A = univ is natural density, |S ∩ [0,b)| / b → α.
(3) Boundary cases. At c = 0 the set is empty, proved in scratch, so f 0 = 0 is forced. At n = 0, 1, log n = 0 gives the junk value 0, which is irrelevant for density. Densities are unique (tendsto_nhds_unique), so f is the density function itself.
(4) The strict `<`, the natural log, the domain c ≥ 0, and continuity on [0,∞) including at 0 all match the source.
(5) The only structural difference is the 0-indexed `primeGap`. It is a proved-equivalent reformulation; see the reformulations entry and /workspace/review/equiv.lean.
(6) The source states an assertion, not a question. The file wraps it as `answer(sorry) ↔ P`, with P having the same polarity as the source's claim, so this is not a negated conjecture — a style choice only.
Status: the file's `research open` agrees with erdosproblems.com (OPEN, 2026-09-23) and with the teorth/erdosproblems database (open). The original Erdős papers behind the site were not consulted; the file cites only erdosproblems.com, and that source was read in full.
